Hi Akari — thanks, happy to run the demo. Quick note on timezones:

- 10:00 JST (Tokyo) = 09:00 SGT (Singapore) = 11:00 AEST (Sydney) *if Sydney is on standard time*.
- Sydney currently observes AEST (UTC+10) but moves to AEDT (UTC+11) for DST later in the year. For July it's AEST, so the mapping above should hold.

I'm looping in Mina (solutions engineer) and Ben (account exec) so we have the right folks. To avoid the common "next-day" calendar confusion between Sydney and Tokyo, can you confirm which city/timezone your attendees are in? Also, could your calendar system be sending invites in local time or dropping the timezone field (we sometimes see external ICS files without TZ data)?

Proposed alternatives (local times in parentheses):
- Option A: Mon 19 Jul 2027 09:00 SGT / 10:00 JST / 11:00 AEST
- Option B: Mon 19 Jul 2027 11:00 SGT / 12:00 JST / 13:00 AEST

If you confirm Option A I'll send an invite with an explicit ICS and a short agenda.

Thanks,

Hiro Tanaka
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com | +81 90-xxxx-xxxx

Hi Hiro — thanks for the breakdown. Apologies, Samir (our Singapore ops lead) and Mei (Sydney) are both joining; their calendars showed different times which caused the confusion.

Samir says his calendar rendered the invite as 09:00 but Mei in Sydney saw it as 00:00 the "next day" (calendar shows Mon 19 Jul 00:00). Samir forwarded the invite and it appears our internal calendar converter may have a bug for events around midnight.

Can you please send the invite with explicit timezone offsets and the event description stating all three local times? That should prevent anyone misreading the event.

Akari
